questions.q: You must ensure modifications to a production server's approved configuration are reviewed, tested, and documented before deployment. Which process governs this?
questions.why: Change management reviews, approves, and documents modifications to baselines before they reach production.

questions.q: You are decommissioning SSDs that held sensitive data. Given wear-leveling, which sanitization method most reliably renders the data unrecoverable?
questions.why: Degaussing does not affect flash, and overwrites miss remapped cells. Cryptographic erase destroys the key so data is unreadable.

questions.q: A user must be able to read and update files in a shared NTFS folder but not delete them or change permissions. Which permission assignment fits?
questions.why: Modify and Full Control both allow deletion. Read & Execute plus Write lets a user open and update files without delete rights.

questions.q: To reduce fraud risk in payment processing, which assignment enforces separation of duties?
choices: One admin holds both create and approve rights for efficiency
Rotate a single operator through all duties weekly
The person who creates a vendor cannot also approve payments to that vendor
questions.why: Separation of duties splits conflicting tasks so no single person can both create a vendor and approve its payments.

questions.q: A critical vendor patch is released for internet-facing servers. What should you do before deploying it broadly?
choices: Test the patch in a staging environment that mirrors production
Deploy immediately to every system to close the window
Wait for the next quarterly window regardless of severity
questions.why: Testing in a representative staging environment catches breakage before a patch hits production systems.

questions.q: You need to verify that servers conform to a hardening baseline such as the CIS Benchmarks. Which tool is appropriate?
choices: A configuration compliance scanner using SCAP
questions.why: SCAP-based compliance scanners check systems against defined benchmarks and report configuration deviations.

questions.q: You must email a document classified as Restricted to an external partner. Which control best satisfies the handling requirement?
choices: Compress the attachment into a ZIP
Encrypt the message and attachment before sending
questions.why: Encryption protects the confidentiality of restricted data in transit; footers and ZIP compression do not secure it.

questions.q: Newly received laptops must be accountable from procurement through disposal. Which practice supports this?
choices: Image them and skip registration to save time
Record only devices that later fail
Track devices only after a security incident
Maintain an asset inventory with unique identifiers and assigned owners
questions.why: A complete asset inventory with unique IDs and owners provides lifecycle accountability for each device.

questions.q: A hospital grants permissions based on job function such as nurse or billing clerk. Which access control model is in use?
questions.why: RBAC assigns permissions to roles that map to job functions, and users inherit access through role membership.

questions.q: In a system enforcing mandatory access control, what determines whether a subject may read an object?
choices: Comparison of the subject's clearance and the object's classification label
Group membership defined by the user
questions.why: MAC decisions compare a subject's clearance to the object's label; owners cannot override the system policy.

questions.q: In Kerberos, after obtaining credentials from the ticket-granting service, what does the client present to a target service?
questions.why: The TGT is used to request service tickets from the TGS; the client then presents the service ticket to the target service.

questions.q: In an 802.1X port-based access control deployment, which component acts as the authenticator?
choices: The network switch or wireless access point
questions.why: The authenticator is the switch or access point that gates the port; the RADIUS server is the authentication server.

questions.q: An employee transfers from Sales to Finance. Which access practice prevents privilege creep?
choices: Revoke old-role entitlements and grant only new-role entitlements
Add Finance rights and keep Sales rights for continuity
Grant temporary domain admin during the transition
Disable the account and recreate it with all prior rights
questions.why: Removing the old role's access when granting the new one keeps entitlements matched to current duties.

questions.q: In a SAML federation, which party issues the assertion that authenticates a user to a service provider?
questions.why: The identity provider authenticates the user and issues the SAML assertion the service provider then trusts.

questions.q: Which account setting best limits online password brute-force attempts while avoiding easy denial of service?
choices: Unlimited login attempts with logging only
Permanent lockout after one failed attempt
A lockout threshold with a reset counter and temporary lockout duration
questions.why: A threshold with automatic reset and temporary lockout slows guessing without permanently locking users out.

questions.q: Which scan gives the most accurate assessment of missing patches on a host?
questions.why: Credentialed scans log in to inspect installed packages and patch levels, yielding far fewer false results.

questions.q: A control's single loss expectancy is $10,000 and the asset is expected to be affected twice per year. What is the annualized loss expectancy?
questions.why: ALE equals SLE times ARO, so $10,000 multiplied by an ARO of 2 equals $20,000.

questions.q: An analyst wants to detect one source IP failing logins across many accounts. Which SIEM capability enables this?
choices: Event correlation across multiple log sources
questions.why: Correlation links related events across sources so a distributed pattern from one IP triggers a single alert.

questions.q: An IDS keeps alerting on traffic from the authorized internal vulnerability scanner. What is the appropriate tuning action?
choices: Block the scanner at the firewall
Create a tuning exception for the scanner's source address
questions.why: Whitelisting the known scanner source suppresses the false positives without weakening overall detection.

questions.q: In CVSS, which metric group describes traits of a vulnerability that do not change over time?
questions.why: Base metrics capture the intrinsic, constant characteristics of a vulnerability, unlike temporal or environmental factors.

questions.q: To keep collected logs trustworthy and tamper-evident, what should you implement on the log server?
choices: Write-once storage with cryptographic hashing of log files
Allow administrators to edit logs for clarity
Store logs only on the monitored host
Rotate logs hourly and delete the originals
questions.why: Write-once media plus hashing lets you prove logs were not altered after collection, supporting integrity.

questions.q: An analyst is alerted because traffic deviates from the learned normal baseline. Which detection method produced this alert?
questions.why: Anomaly detection flags deviations from an established baseline of normal behavior rather than matching known signatures.

questions.q: Following the standard incident response lifecycle, which phase immediately follows containment?
questions.why: The sequence is preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery, then lessons learned.

questions.q: When collecting digital evidence, which data should be captured first according to the order of volatility?
choices: Data on a remote logging server
questions.why: The most volatile data, such as CPU registers and cache, is lost soonest and must be captured first.

questions.q: What must be documented to maintain chain of custody for seized evidence?
choices: Who handled the evidence, when, and for what purpose at each transfer
questions.why: Chain of custody records every handler, time, and reason so the evidence's integrity can be proven.

questions.q: A workstation is actively exfiltrating data to an external host. What is the fastest effective containment step that preserves evidence?
choices: Power it off immediately to stop the process
Isolate the workstation from the network
Run a full antivirus scan first
questions.why: Network isolation stops the exfiltration while preserving volatile memory; powering off or reimaging destroys evidence.

questions.q: A system may lose no more than 15 minutes of data during a recovery. Which metric does this define?
questions.why: RPO defines the maximum acceptable data loss measured back from the disruption, here 15 minutes.

questions.q: A nightly job backs up only files changed since the last full backup and does not clear the archive bit. Which backup type is this?
questions.why: Differential backups capture changes since the last full backup and leave the archive bit set, unlike incremental backups.

questions.q: You need a recovery site with hardware in place and near-real-time data replication for rapid failover. Which site type fits?
questions.why: A hot site is fully equipped and continuously updated, enabling failover in minutes rather than days.

questions.q: Which algorithm is best suited to efficiently encrypt a large volume of data at rest?
questions.why: AES is a fast symmetric cipher ideal for bulk data; RSA, DH, and ECDSA are asymmetric and far slower for volume.

questions.q: MD5 file-integrity hashes are being deprecated due to collisions. Which algorithm is the appropriate replacement?
questions.why: SHA-256 is collision resistant; SHA-1 is also weakened, CRC32 is an error check, and Base64 is only encoding.

questions.q: To provide non-repudiation for a message, with which key does the sender sign it?
questions.why: Signing with the sender's private key binds the message to the sender, since only they hold that key.

questions.q: Which mechanism lets a client check in near real time whether a certificate has been revoked?
questions.why: OCSP queries a responder for the live status of a single certificate; CRLs are periodically published lists.

questions.q: Which protocol lets two parties agree on a shared secret over an insecure channel without transmitting the secret itself?
questions.why: Diffie-Hellman derives a shared secret from exchanged public values without sending the secret over the wire.

questions.q: After a TLS handshake completes, what is the negotiated symmetric session key primarily used for?
questions.why: The symmetric session key encrypts the application data efficiently after asymmetric methods establish it.

questions.q: Why should you add a unique salt to each password before hashing it?
choices: To make the hashes reversible for recovery
To encrypt the password with a shared key
To defeat precomputed rainbow table attacks
questions.why: A unique salt makes each hash distinct so precomputed rainbow tables cannot be reused against them.

questions.q: You must isolate IoT devices from corporate workstations that share the same physical switch. Which control accomplishes this?
questions.why: Separate VLANs create distinct broadcast domains, logically segmenting devices on one physical switch.

questions.q: Which IPsec mode encrypts the entire original IP packet and is typically used for site-to-site VPN gateways?
questions.why: Tunnel mode encapsulates and encrypts the whole original packet, suiting gateway-to-gateway VPNs. Transport protects only the payload.

questions.q: You want internal users to browse HTTPS sites while blocking unsolicited inbound connections on a stateful firewall. Which rule is correct?
choices: Allow outbound and inbound TCP 80 only
Allow outbound TCP 443 and let stateful inspection permit the return traffic
Block all TCP 443 in both directions
questions.why: Permitting outbound 443 lets the stateful firewall track sessions and allow only their return traffic, without opening inbound.

questions.q: You want to replace WPA2-PSK to gain forward secrecy and resistance to offline dictionary attacks. Which should you deploy?
questions.why: WPA3 uses SAE, which provides forward secrecy and resists offline password guessing, unlike WPA2 pre-shared keys.

questions.q: Which technology protects against DNS cache poisoning by validating the authenticity and integrity of DNS records?
questions.why: DNSSEC digitally signs records so resolvers can verify origin and integrity. DoH only encrypts the query transport.

questions.q: Which switch feature restricts which devices may use a port based on authenticated identity?
questions.why: 802.1X requires a device to authenticate before the switch port forwards traffic, blocking unauthorized devices.

questions.q: To capture traffic between two hosts on a switched network for analysis, which switch feature do you enable?
questions.why: A SPAN or mirror port copies traffic from monitored ports to an analyzer, since a switch does not flood unicast.

questions.q: Which coding practice most effectively prevents SQL injection in a web application?
questions.why: Parameterized queries separate code from data so user input cannot alter the SQL statement's structure.

questions.q: Which control most directly mitigates reflected cross-site scripting in a web app?
choices: Output encoding of user-supplied data in the response
questions.why: Encoding user data before it is rendered prevents the browser from executing injected script as markup.

questions.q: Which capability primarily distinguishes EDR from traditional signature-based antivirus?
choices: It only matches signatures of known files
Behavioral detection and response using host telemetry
Blocking based solely on file extensions
Scanning email attachments at the gateway
questions.why: EDR continuously collects endpoint telemetry to detect suspicious behavior and enable investigation and response.

questions.q: To prevent execution of unauthorized binaries on a hardened server, which control is most effective?
questions.why: Allowlisting permits only approved programs to run, blocking unknown or unauthorized binaries by default.

questions.q: Why would you run a suspicious executable inside a sandbox?
choices: To permanently store it for evidence
To sign it with a trusted certificate
To observe its behavior in isolation without risking the host
questions.why: A sandbox contains the sample so analysts can watch what it does without exposing production systems.

questions.q: Which control lets an administrator remotely enforce encryption and wipe corporate data from lost mobile devices?
questions.why: MDM enforces device policies such as encryption and can remotely lock or wipe managed devices.

questions.q: Which security risk is specific to a hypervisor hosting multiple virtual machines?
choices: VM escape that lets a guest reach the host or other VMs
SQL injection in the database tier
questions.why: VM escape breaks the isolation boundary, letting a compromised guest access the hypervisor host or neighboring VMs.
